front_blocks.md: Define **atomic number**.

back_blocks.md: An **atomic number** (*Z*) is the number of **protons** in the nucleus of an atom. It is unique to each element and determines the element's identity.

front_blocks.md: Define **atomic radius**.

back_blocks.md: An **atomic radius** is a measure of the size of an atom. It is defined as half the distance between the **nuclei** of two covalently bonded atoms of the **same element**.

front_blocks.md: Why does a beam of **electrons** deflect more than a beam of **protons** in the same electric field?

back_blocks.md: **Electrons** deflect more because their **mass** (~1/1836 that of a proton) is far smaller. The same electrostatic force produces a much greater acceleration on the lighter electron, causing stronger deflection.

front_blocks.md: Why does **atomic radius decrease** across a period?

back_blocks.md: Across a period, **nuclear charge** increases as more protons are added, but electrons are added to the **same principal quantum shell**. The stronger nuclear pull draws electrons closer to the nucleus, decreasing the **atomic radius**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
In a neutral atom, the **number of electrons** equals the **number of protons**.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
A neutral atom carries no overall charge, so the negatively charged **electrons** must exactly balance the positively charged **protons** in the **nucleus**.

front_blocks.md: Define **mass number**.

back_blocks.md: A **mass number** (*A*) is the total number of **protons** and **neutrons** in the nucleus of an atom. It is also called the **nucleon number**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Atomic **radius** increases across a period as more electrons are added to the outer **shell**.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Atomic **radius decreases** across a period. Although electrons are added to the same shell, the increasing **nuclear charge** pulls electrons closer to the nucleus, reducing the radius.

front_blocks.md: Define **nucleon**.

back_blocks.md: A **nucleon** is a particle found in the **nucleus** of an atom. Both **protons** and **neutrons** are nucleons.

front_blocks.md: A **Cl**<sup>**-**</sup> ion has atomic number 17 and mass number 35. How many **protons**, **neutrons**, and **electrons** does it have?

back_blocks.md: A **Cl**<sup>**-**</sup> ion has:

1. **Protons:** 17 (= atomic number)
2. **Neutrons:** 18 (= 35 − 17)
3. **Electrons:** 18 (= 17 + 1, because Cl<sup>-</sup> has gained 1 electron)

front_blocks.md: Why does **atomic radius increase** down a group?

back_blocks.md: Moving down a group, each element has an additional **principal quantum shell**. Electrons in inner shells **shield** outer electrons from the nuclear charge, weakening the attraction and increasing the **atomic radius**.

front_blocks.md: What happens to a beam of **neutrons** passing through an electric field?

back_blocks.md: A beam of **neutrons** passes straight through **without deflection**. Neutrons carry no charge and are therefore unaffected by the electric field.

cards.front_md: What happens to a beam of **neutrons** passing through an electric field?

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A **Mg**<sup>**2+**</sup> ion (atomic number 12) has 12 **electrons**.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A **Mg**<sup>**2+**</sup> ion has **10 electrons**. Magnesium has atomic number 12, but the 2+ charge means it has **lost 2 electrons**, leaving 10.

front_blocks.md: Why does a **positive ion** have a positive charge?

back_blocks.md: A **positive ion** forms when an atom **loses** one or more electrons. This leaves more **protons** than electrons, so the particle has more positive charge than negative charge, giving it an overall **positive charge**.

cards.front_md: Why does a **positive ion** have a positive charge?
cards.back_md: A **positive ion** forms when an atom **loses** one or more electrons. This leaves more **protons** than electrons, so the particle has more positive charge than negative charge, giving it an overall **positive charge**.

front_blocks.md: Why is a **negative ion** larger than its parent atom?

back_blocks.md: A **negative ion** forms by gaining extra electrons while the **nuclear charge** stays the same. The greater number of electrons experience a weaker pull from the nucleus, so the **ionic radius** increases.

cards.front_md: Why is a **negative ion** larger than its parent atom?
cards.back_md: A **negative ion** forms by gaining extra electrons while the **nuclear charge** stays the same. The greater number of electrons experience a weaker pull from the nucleus, so the **ionic radius** increases.

front_blocks.md: Why does the **nucleus** carry an overall **positive charge**?

back_blocks.md: The **nucleus** contains **protons** (relative charge +1) and **neutrons** (no charge). The positive charges of the protons are unopposed within the nucleus, giving it an overall **positive charge**.

cards.front_md: Why does the **nucleus** carry an overall **positive charge**?

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
All **ions** of the same element have the same number of **protons**.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
The number of **protons** (the **atomic number**) is fixed for a given element and does not change when electrons are gained or lost. Only the number of **electrons** changes when ions form.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

All **ions** of the same element have the same number of **protons**.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

The number of **protons** (the **atomic number**) is fixed for a given element and does not change when electrons are gained or lost. Only the number of **electrons** changes when ions form.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A **Ca**<sup>**2+**</sup> ion is smaller than a neutral **Ca** atom.

back_blocks.md: **True.**

A **Ca**<sup>**2+**</sup> ion has lost 2 electrons while the **nuclear charge** stays the same. Fewer electrons experience a stronger pull, reducing the **ionic radius** compared to the neutral calcium atom.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The **mass** of an atom is concentrated in the **nucleus**.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
**Protons** and **neutrons** each have a relative mass of 1, while the **electron** mass (~1/1836) is negligible. Almost all the mass of an atom is therefore found in the **nucleus**.

front_blocks.md: An unknown atom **X** has mass number 63 and 34 neutrons. How many **protons** does it have, and what element is it?

back_blocks.md: Atom **X** has **29 protons** (= 63 − 34). An element with atomic number 29 is **copper** (Cu).

front_blocks.md: Why does **atomic radius** increase sharply between a **noble gas** and the **alkali metal** that starts the next period?

back_blocks.md: The **alkali metal** at the start of the next period has one extra **principal quantum shell** compared to the noble gas. This additional shell greatly increases **shielding** and distance from the nucleus, causing a sharp rise in **atomic radius**.

front_blocks.md: Define **atom**.

back_blocks.md: An **atom** is the smallest particle of an element that can take part in a **chemical reaction**. It consists of a central **nucleus** containing **protons** and **neutrons**, surrounded by **electrons** in **shells**.

front_blocks.md: In which direction is a beam of **protons** deflected in an electric field?

back_blocks.md: A beam of **protons** is deflected slightly toward the **negative plate**. Protons carry a positive charge and are attracted to the negative plate, but deflect less than electrons due to their much greater **mass**.
